findings.title: canManage() grants manage on view scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). A caller with only the Groups VIEW scope for all-groups therefore passes canManage(), which guards create/update/delete group, add child, and role-mapping endpoints. VIEW must not imply MANAGE; only MANAGE should be checked.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource id instead of group id
findings.body: The loop over findByType uses groupResource.getId() both to evaluate permission and to populate the result set. Resources are stored by group id in the resource name (findByName(server, groupId)), as done in hasPermission() and in the V1 implementation which uses resource.getName(). Using the internal authz resource UUID means the lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups evaluation, and the returned set contains authz UUIDs instead of group IDs. Downstream users search (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, getUsersCount(...,groupIds)) expects group IDs, so filtering is wrong.

findings.title: Possible NPE when all-groups resource does not exist
findings.body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource() which can return null if the type resource is missing, then unconditionally calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). Passing a null resource can throw NPE and break every group permission check. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(). A null check is required before querying policies.
